uncertain.title: `agent: {http2: false}` turns off HTTP/2 session reuse entirely, where the old code pooled one session
uncertain.explanation: Documented source facts: in got 16, `agent.http2` is only an opt-out flag, and `false` skips session pooling. By default got 16 uses a built-in pooled session cache with multiplexing. Code evidence: the old code used `new http2wrapper.Agent({maxSessions: 1})`, which reused one pooled HTTP/2 session. The new `agent: {http2: false}` disables pooling, so each snapshot read (including the retry) may set up a new TLS/HTTP/2 session. That adds latency against the 2500 ms request timeout and puts more connection load on the server. The migration guide's equivalent setup is just `{http2: true}`. Unless turning pooling off is intended, remove the `agent` option to keep session reuse.

reported.title: got v16 throws when agent.http2 is given an agent instance, so readStatus breaks
reported.explanation:
What the code does: `src/client.ts` line 5 creates `relayAgent = new http2wrapper.Agent({maxSessions: 4})`, and line 11 passes it as `agent: {http2: relayAgent}`. Line 10 also passes `request: http2wrapper.auto`. package.json now asks for got ^16.1.0.

What the docs say: the got v16.0.0 breaking-change notes say HTTP/2 support was rewritten and the http2-wrapper dependency was dropped. They also say "`agent.http2` is no longer an agent slot. It is only an opt-out flag now: pass `false` to skip session pooling. Passing an agent instance throws." Got's options docs at a pinned commit agree: `agent.http2` is only a pooling opt-out flag, and custom HTTP/2 agents are not part of the public API.

Result: every health poll through `readStatus` will throw as soon as it runs on got 16. Raising the timeout won't help.

The same notes say that if `options.request` returns a request, that function controls the transport and got's HTTP/2 client is skipped. So keeping `request: http2wrapper.auto` would also skip got's new built-in client.

Fix: remove the `agent.http2` instance and the `request: http2wrapper.auto` override, and rely on got's built-in HTTP/2 client with `http2: true`. You can then remove the http2-wrapper Agent from `closeClient`, and maybe the dependency. The other option is to stay on got ^15 until the migration is done.

reported.title: got v16 throws when an agent instance is passed in `agent.http2`, so readStatus always fails
reported.explanation:
**What the code does:** `src/client.ts` creates `relayAgent = new http2wrapper.Agent({maxSessions: 4})` on line 5. It passes it to got as `agent: {http2: relayAgent}` on line 11, alongside `request: http2wrapper.auto`. `package.json` now asks for `got` ^16.1.0.

**What the docs say:** The got v16.0.0 breaking-changes notes say "`agent.http2` is no longer an agent slot. It is only an opt-out flag now: pass `false` to skip session pooling. Passing an agent instance throws." The same notes say got v16 has its own HTTP/2 client and dropped the `http2-wrapper` dependency. Their migration example tells you to stop passing `request: http2wrapper.auto` and `agent: {http2: new http2wrapper.Agent()}`, and to just use `{http2: true}`.

**Effect:** Every health poll would fail with an options error before any network request is made.

**Fix:** Either keep `got` on ^15, or migrate `src/client.ts` to the v16 API:
- remove `relayAgent`, `request: http2wrapper.auto` and the `agent.http2` setting, and rely on got's built-in HTTP/2 session pool;
- change `closeClient()` to match;
- drop `http2-wrapper` from the dependencies if nothing else uses it.

I'm also not sure got v16 exposes `maxSessions: 4` as a setting, so check that before dropping it.

reported.title: Commander 15 upgrade turns colors off by default, against what the README promises
reported.explanation: Repository facts: src/cli.ts defines both `--no-color` (line 7) and `--color` (line 8), then passes `Boolean(options.color)` to `success()` (line 15). README.md line 4 says "Colors are on by default". bun.lock pins commander@15.0.0. Documented library change: the commander 15.0.0 release notes include this breaking fix: "only lone `--no-*` option sets default option value to `true`, default not implicitly set when define both positive and negative option in either order (#2405)". Inferred effect: on commander 14, defining `--no-color` first made `color` default to true. On 15, because both options are defined, `options.color` stays `undefined` when neither flag is passed. `Boolean(undefined)` is false, so the default output loses its color and the README is no longer accurate. Fix: set the default explicitly, e.g. `.option('--color', 'Enable colors', true)`, or use `options.color !== false`. A test for the no-flag case would catch this.

reported.title: Commander 15 upgrade turns colors off by default when no color flag is passed
reported.explanation: What the code shows: src/cli.ts defines both `.option('--no-color')` and `.option('--color')`, then calls `success(text, Boolean(options.color))`. README.md line 4 says "Colors are on by default". In commander 14, defining `--no-color` first made the default value of `color` true. What the docs say: the v15.0.0 release notes list as Breaking (#2405): "only lone `--no-*` option sets default option value to `true`, default not implicitly set when define both positive and negative option in either order". Result: with commander 15.0.0 (the version locked in bun.lock), running with no color flag leaves `options.color` as `undefined`. `Boolean(undefined)` is `false`, so status lines are printed without color, against the README's stated behavior. Fix: set the default explicitly, e.g. `.option('--no-color', 'Disable colors')` plus `command.setOptionValueWithSource`, or define `.option('--color', 'Enable colors', true)`, or use `options.color !== false`. Adding a test for the no-flag case would catch this.
